memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "God heard their groaning and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob. So God looked on the Israelites and was concerned about them." - Exodus 2:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the darkness of these two chapters, the passage ends with four glorious verbs about God: He heard. He remembered. He looked. He was concerned.

God remembering does not mean He had forgotten. In Scripture, remembering means moving to act on what He has promised. He had made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob generations earlier, and now the time had come.

And why did He act? Not because Israel deserved it, and not because they had earned it by good behaviour — the following chapters show a people who complain constantly. He acted because of His covenant and His compassion. Grace, from beginning to end.

This is the heart of the God we worship. He is not distant. He hears groaning. He looks at suffering. He is concerned.

The same God later looked at a lost world and sent His Son (Jn 3:16). The deliverance beginning here in Exodus points forward to the greater exodus Christ accomplished, leading us out of a slavery far deeper than Egypt's.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I truly believe God hears me and is concerned about my situation?
2. How does God's faithfulness to His covenant strengthen my trust in Christ today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You hear, You see, and You care. Thank You for the greater rescue You accomplished in Jesus. Amen.
